system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: the engine narrows the context down in real-time to what's immediately relevant to each turn of the conversation
system_prompt_style.note: PromptBuilder with named sections; guidelines matched per turn.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: Parlant also uses embedders to create vector representations of text. These are used for semantic retrieval where applicable throughout the response lifecycle.
env_context_strategy.note: Environment is a conversation; retrievers and glossary also inject domain knowledge. Closest value.

context_compaction.note: Engine source for history handling not in the evidence bundle.

observation_format.note: Tool results are ToolResult data objects; rendering format not shown.

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: All LLM requests in Parlant are actually made using these schematic generators, which means that, whatever model you use, it must be able to generate valid JSON schemas consistently.
tool_call_format.note: The tool caller produces structured JSON via schematic generators, not native function calling.

tool_count.note: Tools are user-defined; no built-in tool list in the evidence.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: Tools activate only when their observation matches; they don't sit in the context permanently.
edit_primitive.note: Conversational framework; the README feature list contains no file-editing tool.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: async def query_docs(context: p.ToolContext, user_query: str) -> p.ToolResult:
tool_schema_source.note: Schema is derived from the @p.tool decorated function signature.

protocol_standardization.note: No grep of source for MCP was possible; the file tree was truncated.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: both the human customer and the AI agent are free to add events (messages) to the session at any point in time
loop_primitives.note: Each turn runs a fixed sequence: match guidelines, call tools with optional extra matching iterations, then generate the message.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: Multi-turn SOPs (Standard Operating Procedures). Define a flow for processes like booking, troubleshooting, or onboarding.
planning_granularity.note: Journeys are developer-authored state machines, not model plans. Closest value.

delegation_mechanism.note: A human-handoff doc exists but its content was not included in the evidence.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: Sometimes it makes sense for a human (perhaps a developer) to manually add messages on behalf of the AI agent.
human_in_loop.note: Human agent messages act as steering. Closest value.

short_term_state.note: Sessions track journey states and variables.

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: Embedders: These are used to create vector representations of text for semantic retrieval.
long_term_memory.note: Vector DB adapters exist (chroma, qdrant); customer variables persist across sessions.

state_persistence.evidence_quote: This request adds a new message to a session on behalf of the customer, and triggers the AI agent to respond asynchronously.
state_persistence.note: Sessions are persisted in stores (json_file, mongo) and continue across turns.

termination_condition.note: Runs are per-turn responses; the termination code is not in evidence.

timeouts.note: The long-polling timeout is an API timeout, not an action timeout.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: The same pattern works with LlamaIndex query engines, Agno agents, or any async Python function.
execution_isolation.note: Tools are in-process async Python functions.

permission_model.evidence_quote: Tools activate only when their observation matches; they don't sit in the context permanently.
permission_model.note: Guideline and observation matching gates tool availability.

tracing.evidence_quote: Every decision is traced with OpenTelemetry.

eval_hooks.note: The pytest_stochastics.json test config is not an eval hook; source not inspected.

guardrails.evidence_quote: Moderation Service: This is used to filter out harmful or inappropriate user input in conversations.
guardrails.note: The output filter is strict canned-response composition mode; a lakera adapter also exists.

target_domain.evidence_quote: The conversational control layer for customer-facing AI agents

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: You can also use any model and provider via LiteLLM
